title: Effectiveness of a Nerve Block in the Back of the Head for Treating Headaches Caused by Bleeding in the Brain
official: Efficacy of Bilateral Greater Occipital Nerve Block as a Treatment for Headache Secondary to Spontaneous Subarachnoid Hemorrhage
summary: Main objective: To determine the efficacy of bilateral greater occipital nerve block in the management of headache pain related to SAH

interventions.name: Lidocaína B. Braun 20 mg/ml solución inyectable
Suero Fisiológico Braun 0,9% disolvente para uso parenteral Cloruro de sodio

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Patients with diffuse or perimesencephalic aSAH admitted to the Semicritical Care Unit or ICU of Hospital de la Santa Creu i Sant Pau.
2. Hunt and Hess scale 1-3 (see Annex 3).
3. Signed informed consent from the patient or their representative.
Exclusion criteria:
1. Presence of other causes of secondary headache (AVM, space-occupying lesions, etc.).
2. Pregnancy or breastfeeding.
3. Cardiac conduction disorders: Second- or third-degree atrioventricular block. Arrhythmias with hemodynamic instability.
4. Convexity SAH.
5. Hunt and Hess scale 4 or 5 (see Annex 3).
6. History of allergic reaction to local anesthetic
7. Severe functional dependence (mRS 4-5, see Annex 7).
8. GCS ≤8 prior to the procedure (see Annex 4).
9. Intracranial surgery ≤1 month prior or planned during hospitalization (excluding ventricular drains).
10. Known terminal illness or imminent limitation of therapeutic effort.
11. Difficulty or foreseeable loss of clinical follow-up.
